entities.summary:
Jacques d'Annebaut (Unknown - 1557) was a French cardinal and cousin of Jean Le Veneur, playing a significant role in Western European politics during the 16th century.


He was a member of the powerful Annebaut family, whose connections to the French monarchy influenced his own path. As a cardinal, d'Annebaut held considerable power and influence, navigating the complexities of the Catholic Church and the royal court.


His legacy extends to the French monarchy's development during this period, as he worked closely with King Henry II and later King Francis II.


In his final years, d'Annebaut's influence waned, and he passed away in 1557, leaving behind a complex web of relationships and alliances that shaped the course of Western European history.
